Microsoft starts canceling Claude Code licenses

Thousands of Microsoft developers will use GitHub Copilot CLI instead of Anthropic's Claude Code, according to sources familiar with the matter.

Microsoft first started sending termination notices for Claude Code licenses to employees around the start of May, according to multiple sources familiar with the matter. The company is planning to remove most of its Claude Code licenses by the end of June.

Claude Code, developed by Anthropic, had been adopted by many Microsoft engineers as a supplement to GitHub Copilot. The tool allows developers to interact with their codebase using natural language, generate code, run tests, and commit changes — all from the terminal.

The company is transitioning developers to GitHub Copilot CLI as its primary AI coding assistant for internal development. GitHub Copilot CLI provides similar terminal-based AI assistance and is deeply integrated with Microsoft's existing developer toolchain.

Microsoft's decision reflects broader consolidation of its AI tooling strategy. The company has invested billions of dollars in OpenAI and has been working to unify its AI products under the Copilot brand, spanning Office, Windows, GitHub, and Azure.

Sources say the rollout of Claude Code at Microsoft was substantial, with licenses covering a significant portion of the company's engineering workforce. The exact number of licenses being canceled has not been confirmed, but estimates from sources put the figure in the thousands.

Anthropic confirmed that Microsoft is one of its enterprise customers but declined to comment on specific licensing arrangements. A Microsoft spokesperson said the company is "continuously evaluating its developer tooling portfolio to ensure engineers have access to the most effective and integrated solutions."

The move comes as competition among AI coding assistants intensifies. Competitors including Cursor, Windsurf, and Replit have all launched terminal-based AI coding tools in recent months, with varying degrees of enterprise adoption across the industry.

Engineers who spoke to The Verge expressed mixed feelings about the transition. Some noted that Claude Code's reasoning capabilities — particularly for complex refactoring tasks — were superior to what GitHub Copilot CLI currently offers. Others were indifferent, citing convenience.

Microsoft has not publicly addressed the decision. The Verge reached out to both Microsoft and Anthropic for comment and will update this story if either company responds with an official statement.
